Humanize Olympiad Agents: A Multi-Session Workflow for Olympiad Problem Solving with Solve, Review, Wiki, Verify
items.excerpt: Large language model (LLM) agents are rapidly improving on long-horizon scientific and olympiad tasks. Recent systems have produced a Lean-formalized resolution of the Navier--Stokes problem and autonomous solutions to four open questions in the Erd\H{o}s Conjectures database. Yet neither system releases both its underlying model and complete inference stack. More broadly, a single agent session remains brittle on difficult problems: early errors can propagate, missing domain knowledge can stall progress, and apparent success can mask a misinterpretation or weakening of the original task. We introduce HOA (Humanize Olympiads Agent), an open, flow-level framework that coordinates multiple agent sessions through three complementary feedback channels. First, an independent reviewer evaluates each candidate and provides actionable feedback. Second, a structured wiki supplies task-specific knowledge that may be missing or unreliable in model pretraining. Third, a verifier checks generated Lean proofs against trusted challenge statements. With GPT-5.6 Sol, HOA achieves perfect scores on the IMO, IPhO, and IOI 2026, near-full marks on the IChO 2026 problem set, and solves all 672 problems (100%) on PutnamBench. On the Lean-Eval leaderboard, HOA ranks first, solving 251 of 304 problems (82.6%). We further evaluate HOA with open models. Using Kimi-K3, HOA achieves full scores on the IMO, IPhO, and IOI, and a gold-level score of 97.1% on the IChO. These results closely match the closed-source GPT-5.6 Sol + /Goal baseline on the IMO and IPhO, while exceeding it on the IChO and IOI, demonstrating that systematic feedback can help bridge substantial differences in base-model capability.
items.summary: 本文提出开源多会话工作流 HOA，通过求解、独立评审、结构化 Wiki 和 Lean 验证器三条反馈通道协同多个 LLM 智能体会话，在 IMO、IPhO、IOI、IChO 2026、PutnamBench 与 Lean-Eval 等奥赛及数学基准上取得近满分或领先表现，表明系统性反馈能显著提升长程奥赛问题求解能力并弥合基座模型差距。

items.title: MatQuery: Execution-Grounded Natural-Language Querying over Heterogeneous Materials Databases
items.excerpt: Materials scientists increasingly combine information from several public databases, each with its own interface, schema, units and calculation conventions. MatQuery is a prototype and experimental infrastructure for studying how a natural-language request can be turned into queries over such databases and how the returned values can be interpreted. This report describes what has been built and the preliminary results obtained so far. The prototype holds frozen, self-verifying local copies of six public materials databases (about 10,000 records each), a catalog of declared fields derived from them, a database-independent query representation with an adapter for each database, and an eight-step pipeline in which a language model proposes and deterministic program steps check, execute and assemble. A benchmark generator produces questions whose reference queries are verified by execution on the frozen copies and whose wording is checked by back-translation and review. An evaluation harness runs direct prompting, CHESS and Alpha-SQL on the same frozen basis. Preliminary experiments on an 800-question development set show that direct generation with three demonstrations reaches 82.4% strict execution accuracy (56.5% without demonstrations), that a low-cost scorer selects the exact set of databases for 85.0% of complete requests with well-calibrated probabilities, and that band gaps differ by more than 0.5 eV in 31.6% of composition-matched cross-database clusters. Two pilots show the limits of the current approach: a probe-then-ask policy gave answers rated valid by both reviewers in only 11 of 50 sessions, and only 115 of 300 sampled record pairs could be compared by structure. The complete pipeline is in smoke testing and has not yet been evaluated at scale.
items.summary: TLDR：MatQuery 是一个“执行验证”的自然语言查询原型基础设施，通过大模型提议与确定性程序校验、执行和组装，将跨六个异构材料数据库的请求转化为可执行查询并解释结果，初步在 800 题开发集上达到 82.4% 的严格执行准确率。

items.title: Masked Diffusion Language Agents for Tool-Integrated Chemical Reasoning
items.excerpt: Designing tool-integrated reasoning agent systems for complex chemical tasks remains a fundamental challenge. Although recent chemical agents have demonstrated promising performance through the integration of external tools, they are still built on the autoregressive paradigm, which is inherently constrained by causal attention and left-to-right generation. As a result, they often struggle with bidirectional molecular understanding, global coordinated tool planning and multi-source evidence integration. To address this challenge, we introduce ChemDiffAgent, the first masked diffusion language agent for tool-integrated chemical reasoning. It reformulates chemical reasoning as iterative denoising over interleaved reasoning and tool-use trajectories, enabling tool-use decisions to be jointly determined under full-trajectory context and thereby better aligning the agent's decision boundary with its knowledge boundary. We further analyze how this paradigm benefits agentic reasoning through harder infilling subproblems during training and flexible arbitrary-order decoding during inference. Then we develop a two-stage post-training framework, comprising agentic supervised fine-tuning and variance-reduced preference optimization, to enhance tool-use and reasoning capabilities. We also construct a comprehensive benchmark covering six chemistry tasks across both single-turn and multi-turn tool-use scenarios. Under matched budgets and evaluation, ChemDiffAgent consistently outperforms autoregressive agents, achieving an overall improvement of approximately 20%. Notably, our 8B model achieves performance comparable to, in some cases surpassing, significantly larger frontier models, such as GPT 5.5 and Claude Opus 4.7. Code is available at https://github.com/bilemond/ChemDiffAgent.
items.summary: 本文提出首个用于工具集成化学推理的掩码扩散语言代理 ChemDiffAgent，将推理与工具使用轨迹重构为迭代去噪过程，并借助两阶段后训练，在六项化学任务上较自回归代理平均提升约20%，使8B模型表现可比甚至超越GPT-5.5、Claude Opus 4.7等更大模型。

items.title: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Automated Tuning of Specialized Neural Network Models
items.excerpt: Many machine learning approaches are two-level: an expert selects a class of methods, within this class the choice of key components is critical and usually manual. This paper addresses the automatic tuning of these components and proposes a framework transferable across models of different nature. The multi-agent large language model (LLM) framework has three roles---analyst, coder, and recorder~---with an experiment log and a sandboxed execution environment. Unlike systems that optimize the entire ML script or search architectures in a discrete space, the framework operates over an open but semantically narrow space: the agent generates code only for the specified components, leaving the overall network structure unchanged. The approach is validated in two directions: tuning a classification spiking neural network with correlation learning, and solving high-order differential equations with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN). Across five tasks---spiking classification on MNIST and Digits, and boundary-value problems for the generalized nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (GNLSE) and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky (KS) equations---the agent outperforms the baselines: classification accuracy is 13 percentage points (MNIST) and 6 percentage points (Digits) higher; the error against the analytical single-soliton solution is reduced approximately 2491-fold; the invariant-preservation error drops approximately 325-fold in the selected GNLSE run with a Gaussian perturbation and by more than 100-fold on average over repeated initializations; and the mass drift drops 14-fold for the KS problem with a Gaussian perturbation. The framework thus tunes key components on tasks of different nature without changing its internal structure.
items.summary: 本文提出一个含分析师、编码者和记录者三个角色的多智能体LLM框架，在不改变整体网络结构的前提下自动调优专用神经网络模型的关键组件，并在脉冲神经网络分类与物理信息神经网络求解微分方程等任务上显著超越基线。

items.title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics
items.excerpt: Machine-learning models for perovskite solar cells are typically evaluated using random data splits, which we show systematically leak information through massive internal duplication. Because nearly two-thirds of curated devices share their exact recipe with another, random splits primarily reward the mere recall of historical data rather than testing true physical generalisation. To solve this, we mapped the institutional provenance of the Perovskite Database and established a rigorous hierarchy of grouped splits that progressively isolate duplicate devices, publications, and institutions. Benchmarking thirteen models establishes new state-of-the-art performance across all splits and reveals a critical regime shift: while tree ensembles dominate random splits by recognising familiar recipes, their ranking collapses on genuinely unseen institutions and future discoveries, where composition-aware neural architectures excel. Furthermore, feature importance demonstrates that the device architecture and fabrication methodology dictate final efficiency just as strongly as the absorber chemistry. This standardised protocol empowers the community to separate memorisation from true physical discovery.
items.summary: 该论文揭示钙钛矿光伏机器学习评估中随机数据划分因大量重复配方而泄漏信息、高估记忆能力，并提出按器件、论文和机构来源分组的严格评估协议，通过十三种模型基准测试证明真正泛化到未见机构与未来发现时成分感知神经网络优于树集成，且器件结构与制备方法与吸收层化学同样关键。

items.title: Hindsight Structured Advice Distillation: Steering Executor Agents with Advisors Trained on Their Failures and Task Characteristics
items.excerpt: Language-model agents are used for specialized work such as financial research, healthcare and law. Such agents are often capable enough for a task but still miss its details. In finance, for example, these details include which filing reports a figure or how a company discloses a metric. Retraining the agent to learn these details is expensive, and often impossible when the agent is a closed or shared system. Writing the missing know-how into the agent's prompt makes the prompt long and identical for every input, although different inputs need different guidance. We propose to learn to generate this guidance instead. A small advisor model reads each input and writes structured advice, which is appended to the prompt of a frozen executor. The advisor is trained with hindsight, following work on distillation with privileged information. On a training pool with graded answers, we analyse the executor's failures, run it under several strategies to see which one worked on each input, and let a teacher that sees the grades and the traces write the advice that would have helped. The advisor then learns, by supervised fine-tuning, to write that advice from the input alone. Because the student is a separate small model rather than the executor, it is cheap to train and adds little latency. We call this approach hindsight structured advice distillation (HSAD). On FrontierFinance, a public benchmark of expert-written financial research queries, an 8B advisor raises the qualification rate of Samaya's proprietary research agent, which already leads the benchmark's leaderboard, from 52.9% to 56.6%. This is above the agent's own high-effort configuration, at 37% lower cost per query. We study the generalization of the proposed approach, and in particular show that HSAD also improves results on WebShop, BIRD text-to-SQL and ExpertLongBench.
items.summary: 本文提出 Hindsight Structured Advice Distillation（HSAD），通过让教师模型基于执行器的失败轨迹与评分反向生成有帮助的结构化建议，并监督微调一个小型顾问模型仅根据输入生成建议、再附加到冻结执行器的提示中，从而以低成本提升语言模型代理在金融研究等专业任务上的表现（如在 FrontierFinance 上将资格率从 52.9% 提升至 56.6%，并在 WebShop、BIRD text-to-SQL 和 ExpertLongBench 上也有改进）。

items.title: Faithful and Complete LLM-Assisted Automated Construction of Hierarchical Hardware Knowledge Graphs
items.excerpt: Hardware datasheets contain engineering specifications essential for component selection, system integration, and hardware compatibility verification. However, manual inspection is tedious and error-prone because datasheets are lengthy and heterogeneous, with dense information fragmented across tables, figures, and text. Although large language models (LLMs) can automate this process, na\"ive one-shot processing omits relevant specifications even when the document fits within the model's context window. We present an automated LLM-driven pipeline that transforms hardware datasheets into general-purpose hierarchical hardware knowledge graphs through chunk-based property extraction, hierarchical routing, and iterative refinement. The framework uses LLMs for information extraction and semantic reasoning while preserving source provenance and applying graph updates through validated instructions and deterministic local execution. This staged design reduces per-query context and maintains traceable intermediate representations. The resulting knowledge graphs provide semantically organized, source-grounded hardware properties for downstream retrieval and reasoning. We evaluate the framework on 20 hardware datasheets spanning diverse component types and document lengths. We assess property faithfulness and introduce inter-graph completeness to measure relative semantic coverage without exhaustive ground truth. Our framework achieves 98.8% property faithfulness compared with 76.1% for the one-shot baseline, while fully covering 83.6% of faithful baseline properties; in the reverse direction, the baseline fully covers only 10.5% of ours. These improvements provide more reliable and comprehensive engineering information for downstream hardware design and verification, reducing the risk of overlooked constraints and incorrect decisions.
items.summary: 本文提出一种基于大语言模型的自动化流水线，通过分块属性提取、分层路由和迭代优化，将硬件数据手册构建为可溯源的分层硬件知识图谱，在20个数据手册上实现了98.8%的属性忠实度，并显著优于一次性处理基线（76.1%）。

items.title: Critical Mass: Structure-Disjoint Splits Drift With the Libraries They Are Built On
items.excerpt: Molecular machine learning evaluates out-of-distribution performance with structure disjoint splits, a construction rule fixed once at the scale its library happened to have: threshold a pairwise distance, then assign whole connected components to folds. For predicting structures from mass spectra, the field has converged on single-linkage clustering under the myopic Maximum Common Edge Subgraph (MCES) distance at a threshold of 10. This convention was set on 29,000 molecules but public libraries now hold 227,690 molecules. MCES is NP-hard per pair over a quadratically growing set, and so the criterion has never been evaluated at that scale. We propose an optimized version of this criterion, allowing for computationally feasible application on the public libraries: Admissible bounds and a union-find skip reduce $2.6 \times 10^{10}$ molecular pairs to only $1.15 \times 10^{7}$ integer programs, a $2{,}259\times$ saving, while provably producing the lossless partition. We find that at this scale the graph percolates. A single component holds $95.5\%$ of the library, capping any test set at $4.5\%$. What remains is not merely smaller, but systematically different: a held-out compound outweighs a training compound 88.1\% of the time, because a fixed absolute budget is a tighter relative tolerance on a larger molecule. Large library benchmarks using this splitting rule naively therefore conflate structural novelty with extrapolation to larger, more complex chemistry.
items.summary: 该研究提出可扩展优化方法，首次在22.7万分子公共库上评估质谱分子机器学习常用的MCES距离阈值10结构不相交划分，发现图会渗流（最大连通分量占95.5%，测试集至多4.5%），且留出分子比训练分子更大的概率达88.1%，说明该固定划分规则会随库规模增长而漂移，将结构新颖性与向更大更复杂化学的外推混为一谈。

items.title: Collaborative Learning and Reasoning over Model Slices
items.excerpt: Large language models (LLMs) excel across diverse tasks, benefiting from knowledge priors, in-context reasoning, and test-time computation. Despite these strengths, single-model reasoning remains vulnerable to error propagation, as later steps depend on the model's earlier outputs, leaving reasoning blind spots difficult to independently reassess. To address this limitation, we develop \textit{collaborative learning}, encompassing the construction of heterogeneous collaborators and the learning of effective cross-model collaboration. Specifically, \textit{model slicing} replaces a large model with smaller, heterogeneous models under a comparable parameter budget, enabling prior reasoning to be reassessed across distinct model parameterizations. \textit{Pyramid supervision} combines protocol distillation with step-level supervision to refine reasoning and interaction decisions throughout collaboration. We evaluate our approach across four task categories: multi-hop question answering, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and open-ended constrained generation. The trained heterogeneous models achieve comparable or better task performance than the original large model and established multi-agent baselines, including reinforcement-learning-based methods, while also achieving higher inference efficiency than the multi-agent baselines and exhibiting differentiated collaboration patterns across tasks. These findings show that learned collaboration turns model heterogeneity into complementary reasoning capabilities.
items.summary: 该论文提出通过“模型切片”将大模型替换为同等参数预算下的异构小模型，并用“金字塔监督”学习跨模型协作，从而把模型异构性转化为互补推理能力，在多种任务上以更高推理效率达到或超越原大模型及多智能体基线。

items.title: CB-Orchestrator: Adaptive Workflow Optimization for LLM Agents via Contextual Bandits
items.excerpt: Large Language Model (LLM) agents have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in tackling complex tasks through agentic workflows. However, manually designing these workflows is labor-intensive and lacks flexibility to adapt to diverse queries. While automated workflow optimization is a promising direction, existing methods often incur expensive API costs during training-phase feedback collection. Furthermore, they fail to adaptively reuse high-quality workflows, which creates a bottleneck for both performance and cost-effectiveness. To address these limitations, we propose CB-Orchestrator, an adaptive framework that decouples workflow generation from selection. In the first stage, we construct a diverse pool of candidate workflows via evolutionary search. In the second stage, we formulate workflow selection as a Contextual Bandit problem, which enables sample-efficient learning by balancing exploration and exploitation, thereby significantly reducing the feedback required for training. During inference, the model adaptively selects the optimal workflow tailored to each query. Evaluations across five diverse benchmarks demonstrate that CB-Orchestrator consistently outperforms all baselines. Notably, on the MATH dataset, CB-Orchestrator achieves better performance than strong recent baselines while reducing training-phase API token overhead by no less than 40.55% and total end-to-end training (including workflow pool generation) token overhead by no less than 29.73%.
items.summary: CB-Orchestrator 提出将 LLM 智能体工作流生成与选择解耦的自适应框架：先用进化搜索构建候选工作流池，再用上下文赌博机按查询高效选择最优工作流，从而在多项基准上提升性能并显著降低训练及端到端 API token 开销。

items.title: SpireBench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Strategic Play of Agentic Models with Slay the Spire
items.excerpt: Agentic large language models now tackle complex tasks, yet strategic reasoning over long horizons is under-studied: most agentic benchmarks are short and episodic, and performance on long tasks is hard to dissect into stored knowledge, reasoning and luck. We introduce SpireBench, in which models play the complete commercial deck-builder Slay the Spire (StS), where early decisions decide long-term success. Across 20 large language models (LLMs) at the game's highest difficulty, frontier models beat heuristic baselines and match the average human player but remain far behind experts. This gap widens as the run lengthens: the strongest models win the first act as often as experts, then fall behind. What separates strong models from weak is how well they play each fight; all of them misjudge risk over a run, preserving health rather than spending it to grow stronger. A comprehensive, self-consistent renaming of every game term shows that part of their performance rests on prior knowledge of the game, and models do not improve from the memories they write across runs, which are often wrong and overly cautious. Our harness is the first to give a model the complete original game, and we compare it with existing harnesses. Overall, SpireBench offers an unsaturated long-horizon benchmark with tools to locate where and why agents fail.
items.summary: SpireBench 让 20 个 LLM 在最高难度下完整游玩《杀戮尖塔》，发现其长时程策略表现虽超过启发式基线、接近普通人类却远逊专家，且随游戏推进差距扩大，根源在于战斗决策与风险误判、过度保守以及无法从跨局记忆改进，从而提供了一个可定位智能体长时程失败原因的未饱和基准。

items.title: VIGOR: Verifiable Industrial Geometry Optimization and Repair in Scene Programs
items.excerpt: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate structured layouts and executable scene programs from natural-language instructions. However, executability does not imply engineering feasibility: an industrial scene program may execute successfully while its final state still violates coupled boundary, collision, clearance, aisle, or structural constraints. We identify this mismatch as the executability-engineering-feasibility gap, where locally plausible placements can remain globally infeasible because corrections to one device may introduce violations elsewhere. To make this gap measurable in a controlled setting, we construct an execution-grounded industrial scene-program dataset with 1,749 constructible scenarios, complete executable programs, and 94 final-state geometric checks per scenario. We further propose VIGOR, which combines supervised scene-program generation with execution-grounded verification and staged geometric refinement. Supervised fine-tuning establishes complete program generation, local projection resolves independently correctable violations, and joint conflict-graph repair coordinates residual multi-object conflicts while preserving structural relations. Experiments show that VIGOR achieves 96.86% Complete Feasibility and an Overall score of 91.20, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 10.42 points in Overall. These results show that, under controlled industrial layout conditions, reliable scene-program generation requires not only executable programs, but also explicit verification and coordinated resolution of coupled engineering constraints.
items.summary: 本文提出 VIGOR，通过监督式场景程序生成、执行验证与分阶段几何修复来弥合工业场景程序“可执行但工程不可行”的差距，在 1,749 个场景上达到 96.86% 完整可行性并显著优于基线。

items.title: EliteTable: Self-Improving Program Search for Executable Control Policies
items.excerpt: EliteTable is a self-improving program-search algorithm guided by large language models (LLMs) that uses a fixed-capacity table of high-scoring solutions to guide new proposals, edits of existing solutions, and remixes of several solutions. Performance was evaluated across six Gymnasium control tasks, each with ten generations and fifty candidate slots per generation. Each task was evaluated across ten independently initialized searches. Candidate-score medians rose between the first and final generations in all six tasks, and selected-winner search-score medians rose in five. In CartPole-v1, the selected winner reached the search-score ceiling in the first generation of all ten searches. All ten paired held-out endpoints improved in four of the six tasks. BipedalWalker-v3 and CarRacing-v3 improved without reaching their reporting targets. Six of ten Acrobot-v1 searches declined on held-out episodes, and the median paired change was negative. The results document improvement during program search and the transfer of selected-winner gains to new episodes in some tasks. Comparisons and ablations are needed to establish EliteTable's relative performance and the contributions of its components.

items.title: Humanize MLE Agents: Multi-Agent Session Alternation Beyond Single-Agent Limits
items.excerpt: Existing LLM-based agent approaches for long-horizon machine learning engineering (MLE) often use context engineering, implemented through custom harnesses that manage tools, skills, and accumulated experience. However, we find that as single-session execution lengthens, the agent's reasoning intensity declines alongside slowing progress, summarized as long-horizon deceleration, and the benefits of these custom harnesses vanish as the underlying model improves, summarized as harness staleness. These findings suggest that their benefits may not persist across versions, which motivates a workflow-level approach in which agents build on one another's work across sessions. We model these alternating agent sessions as a context-reset semi-Markov decision process (CR-SMDP) and establish sufficient conditions for alternation to exceed single-agent reference limits, derive an explicit experiment-budget bound, and characterize when session caps preserve this advantage. Guided by this analysis, we introduce Humanize MLE Agents (HMA), which alternates two agents on a shared workspace, limits each session to at most k experiments and resets the context between sessions, without additional task-specific harness or prior knowledge supplements. Across 75 Kaggle tasks in MLE-bench, HMA reaches a state-of-the-art any-medal rate of 78.2%, exceeding the strongest open-source baseline by 8.0 points with a quarter of its time budget. Moreover, among six configurations spanning five heterogeneous agent pairs, HMA improves any-medal rate over the constituent baselines by 6.4 points on average, demonstrating cross-pair generality. A supplementary case on kernel optimization reaches 878 cycles, within 1.6% of the community leaderboard leader, demonstrating applicability beyond MLE.
items.summary: 这篇论文提出 Humanize MLE Agents（HMA），通过两个智能体在共享工作区交替会话、限制每轮实验数并重置上下文，克服单智能体长时 MLE 的推理减速与 harness 过时问题，在 MLE-bench 的 75 个 Kaggle 任务上以 1/4 时间预算达到 78.2% any-medal 的 SOTA，并验证了跨智能体组合与 kernel 优化任务的泛化性。

items.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
items.excerpt: As AI agents increasingly rely on external tools, accurate retrieval is essential for reliable behavior. Existing methods optimize semantic relevance but largely ignore tool availability during execution. To address this gap, we propose RATED (Reliability-Aware Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics), a retrieval framework that combines robust semantic matching with dynamic reliability adaptation. RATED employs a frozen dual-encoder with contrastive fine-tuning for semantic matching, and a lightweight contextual bandit module that re-ranks candidates based on real-time execution feedback. This design enables rapid adaptation to runtime tool failures without expensive model retraining. We introduce EcoAgent, a benchmark of 5,172 real-world tools and over 210,000 query-tool pairs for offline retrieval and dynamic reliability evaluation. Experimental results demonstrate that RATED achieves a 52.2% relative MRR improvement over the ToolLLM API retriever on real-world queries, and reduces fault selection rate from 86.2% to 2.9% under severe API outage scenarios with a 30% failure rate, while incurring negligible latency overhead of less than 1 ms over encode-only inference. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Elliotes/EcoAgent.
items.summary: 该论文提出 RATED——一种结合语义匹配与基于执行反馈的动态可靠性重排的 AI 智能体工具检索框架，可在无需重新训练的情况下快速适应运行时工具故障，并在真实查询和严重 API 故障场景中显著提升检索可靠性。

items.title: Designing Protein Structures from Natural Language
items.excerpt: A central challenge in de novo protein design is generating proteins with desired structural and functional properties. Existing design models typically require a dedicated input representation for each property, limiting the design objectives they support. We develop Prompteina, the first all-atom structure generation model that supports new and broader design objectives specified in natural language, analogous to text-to-image generation. To train Prompteina, we construct Prompteina-Data, a paired text--protein structure dataset of 1.8M structures and 50M+ captions describing global and residue-specific structural and functional properties. We adapt Proteina-Complexa, a pretrained structure generation model, through text-conditioned pretraining and finetuning that aligns residues with their corresponding text. Prompteina outperforms baselines on 15 of 18 structural properties and generates proteins that more closely match descriptions of their intended functions. In binder design, it leads baselines on at least 13 of 20 targets and improves interface confidence by 14\% over the strongest baseline. With iterative in silico feedback, Prompteina's gain over non-iterative generation is 57\% larger than the next-best baseline on the hardest targets. Finally, we experimentally validate Prompteina designs against GM2A, a target with no reported de novo binders. We identify nine binders, with the strongest at an apparent $K_{\mathrm{D}}$ of 107 nM. These results establish natural language as an effective and powerful conditioning interface for protein structure generation.
items.summary: 该论文提出 Prompteina——首个支持以自然语言指定更广泛设计目标的全体原子蛋白质结构生成模型，并构建大规模文本-结构配对数据集进行训练，在多种结构性质与结合体设计中优于基线，且实验验证了针对 GM2A 的纳摩尔级从头结合体。

items.title: Quality, Not Just Outcome: A Structural Scoring Framework for Selecting Coding-Agent Trajectories for Supervised Fine-Tuning
items.excerpt: Open coding agents are commonly trained through supervised fine-tuning on interaction trajectories whose final patches pass the benchmark test suite. However, this outcome-level filtering criterion ignores process quality: trajectories that eventually succeed may still contain inefficient interaction patterns such as repetitive file inspection, unstable tool usage, or delayed modification behavior, all of which become part of the imitation target. We propose TQS (Trajectory Quality Score), a structural scoring framework for coding-agent trajectories that operates directly on trajectory structure, requires no LLM judge, and runs in linear time. TQS characterizes trajectory quality through structural signals organized around structured convergence: information focus, intent--action alignment, and policy dynamics. Using 155,144 successful trajectories from a public open-license corpus, we rank trajectories by TQS and fine-tune coding agents on filtered subsets. Models trained on top-ranked trajectories consistently outperform those trained on random or bottom-ranked subsets on SWE-Bench-Verified. Our results suggest that process-level trajectory quality is an important factor in coding-agent supervision and that structural trajectory filtering provides an effective and scalable alternative to LLM-based data selection.
items.summary: 提出无需LLM评判、线性时间运行的结构化轨迹质量评分框架TQS，从信息聚焦、意图-行动对齐和策略动态等过程信号筛选编码代理的成功轨迹用于监督微调，在SWE-Bench-Verified上优于随机或低质量轨迹训练，表明过程质量而非仅最终结果对编码代理监督至关重要。

items.title: Quantitative Eshelby stability: local and finite-shape theory through AI-assisted mechanics
items.excerpt: How can human researchers use artificial intelligence (AI) to make progress on difficult mechanics problems while retaining control of physical significance, mathematical rigor, and validation? We explore this opportunity through a quantitative stability problem rooted in the Eshelby conjecture. For a uniform dilatational eigenstrain in a homogeneous isotropic solid, we establish a nonlinear two-sided relation between whole-interior strain heterogeneity and a geometry-only distance from the ellipsoid family, with half-order Sobolev scaling that captures morphological length scale. We then develop a complementary finite-shape theory: ellipsoidal subtraction yields an exact residual-field budget from which systematically convergent upper and lower bounds are obtained for a prescribed geometry. Applied to protruded, indented, and necked inclusions, the bounds agree with independent displacement-based finite-element calculations. The study also documents a human-led, AI-assisted research process in which researchers select consequential problems, shape targets, audit arguments, require independent checks, and interpret mechanics, while AI broadens analytical exploration and supports computation. This experience also led us to develop Open Problems in Mechanics, a versioned community-facing map that makes selected mechanics questions, their known/open boundaries, and criteria for progress explicit.
items.summary: 本文以AI辅助力学方式研究Eshelby猜想中的定量稳定性，建立了内部应变非均匀性与偏离椭球族几何距离之间的局部非线性双向关系及可收敛上下界的有限形状理论，并用有限元验证，同时展示了人类主导、AI辅助扩展探索的研究范式。

items.title: JANUS: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models
items.excerpt: Long-horizon autonomous research has shown promise in accelerating scientific progress through sustained cycles of hypothesis generation, implementation, and validation. However, this Generate-Execute-Feedback paradigm relies on reactive trial-and-error, where costly and time-consuming executions introduce severe feedback delays, throttling evolutionary progress under explosively expanding search space. To address this challenge, we propose JANUS, a framework that unifies future outcomes forecasting and past experience reflection through a Predict-Verify-Evolve loop driven by a co-evolving world model. Within an evolving graph, the research agent proposes candidates while world model scores them by forecasting value improvement, information gain, and exploration utility, then accordingly selects, refines, or prunes branches prior to execution. After receiving ground-truth feedback, JANUS distills experience into evolving skills: hierarchical skills for research agent, exploration-strategy skills for world model, and their coordination protocols. This mechanism enables continual co-evolution: the research agent sharpens candidate generation while the world model refines its predictive judgment over extended horizons. Extensive evaluations on MLS-Bench-Lite and real research tasks demonstrate that JANUS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving both higher evolving efficiency and ceiling.
items.summary: 本文提出 JANUS，通过共同演化世界模型驱动的“预测-验证-演化”闭环，在执行前评估并筛选研究候选，并利用真实反馈持续蒸馏技能，使研究智能体与世界模型协同进化，从而显著提升长周期自主研究的效率与上限。

items.title: The 3rd International Workshop on Artificial Intelligence for the Science of Science
Breaking Bottlenecks in Solid Electrolyte Discovery With Large Artificial Intelligence Models
items.excerpt: ABSTRACT Solid electrolytes (SEs) are central to next-generation metal batteries, yet their discovery remains constrained by fragmented data, limited transferability of simulations, and slow experimental iteration. Unlike catalysis, where surface reactivity dominates, SEs require simultaneous optimization of bulk ion transport, defect chemistry, mechanical integrity, and interfacial stability. Here, we outline a framework for autonomous SE discovery enabled by large artificial intelligence (AI) models, including machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) and large language models (LLMs). We discuss the evolution from static materials databases to dynamic, self-updating knowledge systems, the role of MLIPs in bridging density functional theory (DFT) and long-timescale ion migration, and the emergence of LLMs as engines for literature mining, hypothesis generation, and scientific reasoning. We further describe a closed-loop architecture integrating AI-driven candidate design, multiscale simulation, uncertainty-aware selection, and experimental validation. Such systems shift SE research from intuition-guided exploration to data-informed, self-improving cycles. We conclude by highlighting challenges in data standardization, interfacial complexity, and reproducibility, and we propose design principles for building autonomous laboratories for solid-state battery materials.

items.excerpt: ABSTRACT Anti-counterfeiting technologies are increasingly challenged by advances in imaging and machine learning, exposing the fundamental limitations of conventional static optical security systems. Here, a time-resolved physically unclonable function (TR-PUF) system is established, transforming optical authentication from static pattern recognition to high-dimensional temporal encoding. Central to this approach, boron-based room-temperature phosphorescent (RTP) materials are developed via covalent coupling with coumarin derivatives using a solvent-free strategy that is readily scalable to kilogram-level production, exhibiting a maximum phosphorescence lifetime of over 2 s, an ultralong afterglow visible for up to 30 s, and color-tunable emission. The formation of rigid B-O-C linkages spatially isolates emissive centers, suppressing energy transfer and preserving temporally independent decay channels-an essential prerequisite for high-entropy time-resolved encoding. Randomly embedding these multi-emissive RTP units into a polymer matrix forms a complex encryption structure that enables a dual-entropy encoding mechanism with both spectral and temporal dimensions, generating dynamic time keys for authentication. Moreover, we propose a matched time-gated authentication framework that achieves >99% identification accuracy within 1.2 s while exhibiting resistance against the tested generative machine-learning attacks. This work proposes a practical materials platform and a time-gated authentication strategy, offering a scalable technological path for the development of dynamic optical encryption tags.

items.title: Large Language Model Directed Iteration for the Design of Ultra-Stable Sodium-Ion Battery
items.excerpt: ABSTRACT Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into materials discovery is hindered by the trade-off between exploration breadth and exploitation depth, while the lack of embedded domain knowledge and systematic chemical space compression further limits intelligent materials exploration under data scarcity. Herein, we propose a literature-knowledge-directed iterative workflow that combines large language models (LLMs) with Bayesian optimization (BO) for the rational electrolyte design for ultra-stable sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). LLMs serve as auxiliary tools for knowledge mining, while BO accelerates multi-objective optimization to obtain electrolyte compositions. The optimized dual-anion hybrid solvation electrolyte (DHSE) constructs a synergistic solvation structure, which induces the formation of a compact, inorganic-rich, and mechanically robust cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI). The as-formed CEI layer suppresses parasitic side reactions and accelerates Na + transport by reducing the desolvation barrier. Remarkably, industrial-scale Ah-level hard carbon||NaNi 0.3 Mn 0.3 Fe 0.3 O 2 pouch cells assembled with DHSE deliver a high energy density of 107.7 Wh kg −1 , alongside a superior capacity retention of 94% after 100 cycles at 0.5C. This work not only develops a high-performance electrolyte for practically applicable SIBs but also provides a general human-agent collaborative framework for intelligent materials development under data-limited conditions.

items.title: Optimizing NiMo Electrocatalyst Coatings for Hydrogen Evolution in Alkaline Electrolysis With The Machine Learning-Guided Autonomous Platform CatBot
items.excerpt: ABSTRACT The discovery of efficient, durable, and platinum group metal-free electrocatalysts for alkaline water electrolysis is essential to reduce the cost of green hydrogen. Efficient exploration of the vast possible synthetic space is nevertheless hindered by the slow pace of manual experimentation. Here, a closed-loop optimization is presented that combines an automated electrocatalyst synthesis and testing system, CatBot, with Bayesian optimization and accelerated stress testing at industrial conditions for the rapid discovery of active and durable NiMo coatings. Distinct regions with exceptionally high activity and stability are identified within limited experimental budgets on a nickel wire substrate, using different search strategies to efficiently navigate the six-dimensional synthesis space exceeding possible combinations. The most promising coatings are upscaled onto technological nickel foam electrodes showing platinum-level catalytic activity with overpotentials of 173 mV at -1 in 30 wt.% KOH at for the hydrogen evolution reaction. This work establishes a generalizable strategy for the autonomous optimization of functional electrocatalyst coatings under realistic operating conditions.
items.summary: 本文结合自动化电催化剂合成与测试系统CatBot、贝叶斯优化及工业条件下的加速应力测试，在镍丝基底上对NiMo涂层开展了闭环优化，并将表现最优的涂层放大到镍泡沫电极上。该工作为在实际工况下自主优化功能性电催化剂涂层提供了一种可推广的策略，但相关性能与耐久性结论仍需依据原文实验条件和验证范围加以审视。

items.excerpt: ABSTRACT Manganese-based layered oxides are promising cathodes for sodium-ion batteries, yet their practical deployment is restricted by Mn 3+ -induced Jahn-Teller distortion, irreversible high-voltage P2-O2 phase transitions, and oxygen-related side reactions that collectively cause structural deterioration and rapid capacity fading. Here, based on literature-correlation analysis of reported Ni─Mn P2-type cathodes, we establish a machine-learning-guided dopant-class design strategy. The analysis reveals distinct roles of metal, non-metal, and metalloid dopants in governing cycling stability and redox reversibility, identifying metalloid regulation as the most favorable direction for enhancing high-voltage structural and redox stability. Guided by this insight, an Al─B─F co-doped P2-type cathode is rationally designed, in which boron reinforces the oxygen framework through strong B─O covalency, while Al and F provide complementary cationic and anionic regulation. The optimized cathode delivers 142.8 mAh g −1 at a high average voltage of 3.53 V and exhibits superior low-temperature capacity retention of 98.19% after 300 cycles at −5 C. In situ XRD, soft x-ray absorption spectroscopy, ex situ XPS, operando DEMS, and DFT calculations reveal a highly reversible reaction pathway featuring stabilized oxygen redox and near-zero volumetric strain (ΔV/V ≈ 0.025%). This work establishes machine-learning-guided dopant-class design as a general strategy for developing durable high-voltage layered sodium-ion cathodes.

items.excerpt: ABSTRACT The deployment of 5G/6G communication systems demands microwave dielectric ceramics that simultaneously possess a near-zero temperature coefficient of resonant frequency and an ultra-low dielectric loss (tan δ ), which represents a long-standing challenge that demands effective optimization strategies. Herein, the fundamental limitation is substantially alleviated by a strategy integrating interpretable machine learning with entropy engineering, enabling the reverse design of a medium-entropy perovskite microwave ceramic composition (Ca 0.7 Sm 0.27 Nd 0.03 )[Ti 0.686 (Mg 1/3 Nb 2/3 ) 0.014 Al 0.3 ]O 3 . Multiscale characterization reveals that entropy-induced chemical disorder creates isolated polar nanoregions that pin charged defects, transforming them from a source of relaxation loss into static structural units, which is different from the conventional defect-loss correlation mechanism. The optimized ceramic is implemented in a dielectric resonator antenna, which demonstrates superior performance: a radiation efficiency of 96.2% and a gain of 6.06 dBi. The findings establish a generalizable framework for navigating complex compositional spaces and resolving conflicting properties in perovskite materials.

items.title: Do LLMs Read for Free? Auditing the Open Access Bias in AI-Mediated Science
items.excerpt: How large language models affect various social activities has been widely discussed; however, how large language models themselves influence the mechanisms of scientific knowledge production remains unclear. To investigate this question, this paper designs a quasi-experimental study based on a large-scale bibliometric dataset. Using a Difference-in-Differences model and analyzing citation records from 64,841 articles across 120 communication journals, we find that the emergence of large language models is associated with a widening of the visibility gap between Open Access (OA) and non-OA articles. Specifically, OA articles experienced a significant post-ChatGPT citation acceleration of approximately 0.84% per month, accumulating to roughly 10% over 12 months. Importantly, this estimate represents a conservative lower bound, as gradual LLM adoption and journal review lags attenuate the measured treatment intensity. The findings are consistent with the view that, while LLMs may promote knowledge dissemination, they also risk exacerbating inequality in academic knowledge production—though the precise mechanism behind this pattern remains an important direction for future research.
items.summary: 本文利用120种传播学期刊中64,841篇文章的引文记录并采用双重差分模型，发现大型语言模型出现后开放获取与非开放获取文章之间的可见度差距有所扩大，其中开放获取文章在ChatGPT发布后每月引文增速约提高0.84%，12个月累计约10%，作者称该估计为保守下界。该结果可用于提示科研界和期刊政策制定者关注大型语言模型可能加剧学术知识生产不平等，但原文仅报告关联而非因果机制，且明确机制仍有待未来研究。

Large-scale identical-location electron microscopy enables quantifying nanoparticulate electrocatalyst degradation
items.excerpt: Abstract Fuel cells convert chemical energy into electricity, and their performance relies on electrocatalysts whose durability during operation remains poorly understood. Deep mechanistic insight into electrocatalyst stability is essential to design durable, resource-efficient fuel cells. Nanoparticulate electrocatalysts degrade via diverse nanoscale processes, yet particle-to-particle heterogeneity in structure, support interaction, and local microenvironment make true particle-level quantification and understanding impossible with classical approaches. Here we scale up identical-location scanning transmission electron microscopy, which repeatedly images the very same nanoparticles, to track the structural evolution of hundreds of carbon-supported platinum-cobalt nanoparticles, a prototypical oxygen reduction reaction electrocatalyst. We present a three-step image analysis workflow comprising segmentation, tracking, and degradation-event classification with progressive automation, including machine-learning-assisted detection of overlapping particles. By pairing nanoscale resolution and local history with population-level statistics, the pipeline enables unbiased identification and quantification of degradation pathways across statistically meaningful particle sets. We reveal particle size- and shape-dependent effects, showing that smaller and irregular nanoparticles are more prone to detachment, and provide a data-driven framework for probing electrocatalyst degradation at scale.

Towards Physically Grounded Articulated 3D Assets: A Multi-Agent Pipeline and Benchmark
items.excerpt: In this paper, we study physically grounded articulated 3D asset generation---moving the goal from reproducing how objects look to capturing how they move and function. Inspired by the literature on procedural and agentic generation, we present Artisan, a system that extends the latest method Articraft by introducing a multi-agent pipeline with physical simulation feedback, enabling comprehensive attributes beyond geometry, appearance, and physically plausible articulation, such as collision-free motion, stability under gravity, and accurate mass and material properties. Furthermore, we construct a unified benchmark spanning four key aspects: spatial fidelity, physical plausibility, downstream task performance, and overall quality. The benchmark encompasses 100 reference assets from ArtVIP and LightWheel, 50 stability prompts, and 50 ABO objects with reference masses, with protocols evaluating various metrics. Through extensive evaluation of more than 10 representative models, Artisan achieves competitive spatial fidelity while attaining the lowest collision rates and highest stability rates among the evaluated methods. Together, our system and benchmark establish insights for advancing 3D generation towards physically plausible, functionally usable assets.

items.title: Chronos Policy: Learning Robot Policies on Physical Time
items.excerpt: Robot policies often convert sensing and control into fixed-rate observation-action sequences, leaving physical time implicit in sequence position. This assumption breaks when observation rates or delays vary, or when inference latency changes. We introduce Chronos Policy, which makes physical time explicit by conditioning on observation capture times and desired action execution times. We study two ways to incorporate time into a diffusion transformer: adding timestamp embeddings to token features, or encoding physical time in positional encoding through time-aware rotary positional encodings (time-aware RoPE). We find that time-aware RoPE is more robust, allowing attention to depend directly on physical time while keeping token content unchanged. During training, we temporally randomize which observations are sampled and when the action chunk begins, exposing the policy to a wider range of sensing and execution schedules that may occur during deployments. This also enables learning from asynchronous, multi-rate data without forcing all measurements onto a fixed temporal grid. Across simulation and real-world experiments, Chronos Policy improves performance on dynamic tasks, where observation-to-action timing is critical, and on multisensory tasks, where the relative timing between observations matters. On standard quasi-static tasks, it preserves nominal performance while improving robustness to changes in sensing and inference timing.
items.summary: 本文提出Chronos Policy，将观测采集时间和动作执行时间显式编码为策略输入，并采用时间感知旋转位置编码（time-aware RoPE）替代基于序列位置的位置编码，同时通过对训练中观测采样和动作块起点的时序随机化，使策略能从异步、多速率数据中学习而无需对齐到固定时间网格。该工作面向动态任务、多传感器任务和准静态任务，声称可提升对传感与推理时序变化的鲁棒性；但这些性能结论来自原文报告，属于公开材料中的声明，未在本摘要中独立验证。

items.title: Necessary conditions for benchmarking next-generation AI in materials discovery
items.excerpt: Current AI predicts materials by speeding up energy minimisation and training on large databases. However, scaling data generation prevents manual analysis by domain experts. If novelty is evaluated by chemical compositions or traditional representations in Crystallographic Information Files, or standard structure matchers based on manually chosen thresholds, one can easily generate millions of ``new'' compositions or files without discovering truly novel materials. This paper uses a hierarchy of crystal invariants to continuously trace and quantify structural novelty based on the new mathematical definition of a crystal structure and asymptotic guarantees for invariant descriptors. The invariant-based analysis through cascade computations on a modest computer exposes the unexpected scale of duplication in the world's largest materials databases, shown here in the high-profile case of GNoME datasets. To prevent current ``embarrassment of over-prediction'', we propose necessary conditions for next-generation AI that should be automatically enforced before claiming any new materials.
items.summary: 该论文通过晶体不变量连续追踪并量化结构新颖性，揭示包括 GNoME 在内的大型材料数据库存在大量重复，并提出下一代材料发现 AI 在宣称发现新材料前必须自动满足的必要条件。

items.title: Doubly Metastable Synthesis for Accelerated Quantum Materials Discovery
items.excerpt: New physics emerges from new materials, which in turn rely on the development of new synthesis techniques. Identifying the enlargement of metastable synthesis window as enabling for realizing novel materials, we develop diffusion-activated epitaxy, a technique which combines two metastable synthesis methods of diffusion and epitaxy. We observe that within a narrow window of investigated synthesis space we can experimentally identify the stabilization of four distinct phases, three of which show X-ray diffraction and scanning transmission electron microscopy characterization data that are incompatible with the crystal structures registered in experimental and computational inorganic structure databases. These results suggest an enlarged metastable synthesis window is enabled by this synthesis approach, identifying doubly metastable synthesis as a promising method for exploration of quantum materials.

items.title: ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State
items.excerpt: State-space models (SSMs) maintain a fixed-size recurrent state, but reading and writing it at every decoding step can bottleneck hybrid models. This eager state management causes large state I/O with low arithmetic intensity, leaves speculative decoding no cheap rollback, and feeds state quantization error into subsequent recurrent updates. We introduce ReplaySSM, which unrolls the recurrence to represent the state as a checkpoint and a buffer of recent SSM inputs. This separates output computation from checkpoint updates. By updating the checkpoint periodically, ReplaySSM avoids state writes on most steps and roughly halves the dominant state memory traffic. Keeping recent inputs also makes speculative rollback a buffer-pointer operation and enables output-only verification without materializing intermediate states. The same separation allows a low-precision checkpoint to serve output computation on most steps while a higher-precision checkpoint serves recurrent updates, so rounding error in the low-precision copy never enters later updates. We implement ReplaySSM in vLLM for Mamba-2 and Gated DeltaNet. At serving batch size 256, it accelerates standard decoding by $1.20$--$1.47\times$ over a tuned vLLM baseline across four hybrid models, and delivers about $1.8\times$ the throughput of vLLM's speculative decoding on the two 120B-class models. Separate state precisions also reduce output KL divergence and downstream accuracy losses compared with a shared low-precision checkpoint.
items.summary: ReplaySSM 将 SSM 状态表示为检查点加近期输入缓冲区，从而在多数解码步骤避免完整状态写入、以缓冲区指针实现投机回滚，并允许输出计算与循环更新使用不同精度的检查点。该设计在 vLLM 中面向 Mamba-2 和 Gated DeltaNet 实现，摘要报告其在服务批次 256 下相对调优基线加速标准解码，并提升投机解码吞吐、降低输出 KL 散度与下游精度损失；但这些性能与精度结果来自公开摘要所述，尚未经独立验证。

items.title: Sonic-AMG: Streaming Human Motion Generation from Spatial Audio
items.excerpt: Modeling human reactions to spatial audio requires understanding both what is heard and where it comes from. Prior work generates motion offline from complete acoustic and spatial input sequences. Humans, however, react to sounds without knowing what they will hear next. We present Sonic-AMG, to our knowledge the first framework for streaming human motion generation from spatial audio. The model encodes acoustic content and body-relative source geometry as separate tokens. Conditioned on these tokens, a causal transformer with a flow head generates continuous motion latents, from which a causal decoder reconstructs motion segments. Standard teacher-forced training derives motion histories and body-relative source locations from ground-truth motion, whereas streaming inference relies on generated motion for both, resulting in a training-inference mismatch. To reduce this history discrepancy, we introduce rehearsal training, which combines full-sequence teacher-forced supervision with supervised prediction along short autoregressive self-rollouts. To keep spatial conditioning consistent with generated motion, we propose spatial feedback, which recomputes body-relative source locations from generated root poses during both rehearsal training and inference. On SAM, Sonic-AMG achieves state-of-the-art FID and R-precision. It further supports real-time online generation of coherent reactions across sound events and source locations. items.title: Quantitative modeling of acid-base equilibria
items.excerpt: Simulating acid-base equilibria from first principles is a tremendous challenge, as it requires modeling bond-breaking events in a complex hydrogen-bonding environment. The quantum mechanical behavior of the protons is often important, complicating simulations even further. We show that by combining state-of-the-art machine-learning potentials, accelerated sampling of the dissociation process, and an efficient estimation of nuclear quantum corrections it is possible to reliably compute the dissociation constants of different species in water. We demonstrate the transferability of this workflow, applying it successfully to the autoionization of water and to the entire ladder of the aqueous dissociation of phosphoric acid. The definition of the dissociation constant, the choice of order parameters, sampling artifacts and finite-size effects, as well as quantum nuclear effects all play a non-trivial role in determining the outcome of the calculation, so that cutting corners is likely to introduce biases that can only be compensated by fortuitous cancellations of errors.
items.summary: 本文结合先进的机器学习势、加速解离过程采样以及核量子修正的高效估计，提出了一个可从第一性原理可靠计算水中不同物种解离常数的工作流程，并成功将其应用于水的自电离和磷酸在水中的全部逐级解离。该工作表明解离常数的定义、序参量选择、采样伪影、有限尺寸效应和量子核效应都会对计算结果产生重要影响，因此在实际科研中简化处理可能引入偏差，只有在偶然误差抵消时才可能被补偿。

Specialized machine learning force fields for materials dynamics
items.excerpt: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are transforming atomistic simulations by accessing unprecedented length and time scales. While pretrained equivariant graph neural networks achieve robust zero-shot performance for near-equilibrium properties across broad chemical spaces, their translation to complex materials dynamics remains fundamentally challenged by out-of-distribution reactive states, representation biases, and computational scaling limits. In this Review, we examine how physics-driven specialization extends the applicability of MLIPs to complex dynamical systems. We systematically evaluate the structural trade-offs in MLIP design: the undersampling of highly strained configurations, the prohibitive computational overhead of high-order message-passing architectures, and the necessity of nonlocal interactions for open and field-coupled systems. Through four demanding application contexts - electrified interfaces, compositionally fluctuating open systems, multiphase evolution, and large-scale fracture - we establish a framework for observable-specific validation. Highlighting the complementary roles of universal foundation models and task-specific potentials, we emphasize that targeted adaptations must be rigorously benchmarked against intended observables. We conclude with a roadmap for developing physically consistent, hardware-aware force fields that seamlessly connect electronic-structure accuracy to macroscopic materials phenomena.
items.summary: 这篇综述主张，为应对复杂材料动力学中的分布外反应态、表示偏差和计算瓶颈，机器学习原子间势必须从通用预训练模型走向面向特定观测量和物理约束的专用化设计，并建立严格基准与硬件感知路线图，以连接电子结构精度与宏观材料行为。

items.title: Zatom-2: Multitask Pretraining on Atomistic Data for Generative Modeling across Domains
items.excerpt: Unified atomistic modeling has the potential to accelerate discovery in chemistry, materials science, and biology by bridging data-rich chemical domains and data-scarce biological contexts. However, existing generative approaches to atomistic modeling remain highly specialized to scientific disciplines (chemistry vs. biology) or do not leverage both high-volume organic (molecule) and inorganic (material) data for general-purpose pretraining. To this end, we introduce Zatom-2, an atomistic generative model pretrained on approximately five million structures from the OMol25 and OMat24 electronic structure datasets. Zatom-2 features a multiscale Transformer architecture coupled with conditional flow matching that supports force conditioning and foundational pretraining tasks such as generation, structure prediction, and prediction of molecular and material energies and forces. Empirically, Zatom-2 achieves better molecular distribution fidelity than Zatom-1 and achieves strong performance on existing molecule and material generation benchmarks. Zatom-2 demonstrates the ability to control sample generation across low- and high-force regimes, and enhances protein generation in a low-data setting through joint generative-predictive pretraining and transfer learning, increasing protein backbone designability in a length extrapolation setting from 67.8% without pretraining to 74.8% after finetuning on 2,000 protein domains.

items.title: EvoSim: Learning to Model, Modeling to Learn
items.excerpt: Physics-based models connect scientific explanation with quantitative prediction. Constructing them requires selecting physical processes, defining states and governing equations, specifying couplings, and identifying parameters from experiments. Existing AI systems remain limited in making these model structure decisions autonomously. We introduce EvoSim, a self-evolving AI scientist for physical modeling. It uses experimental discrepancies to drive mechanism and equation revisions and held-out experimental data to test physical plausibility. Exploration traces make updates to knowledge, skills, and multi-agent orchestration. This co-evolution improves physics-based models and EvoSim's ability to select mechanisms, diagnose failures, and coordinate research. We evaluate EvoSim on two industrial battery modeling tasks. It predicts lithium-metal-plating onset from 25 to 45 degrees Celsius and 2 C to 6 C with a mean absolute error of 1.79% in state of charge. Dynamic voltage prediction under vehicle driving conditions achieves a root mean square error of 7.62 mV, surpassing the reported accuracy of models developed by human experts. Self-evolution reduces model and physics errors by approximately 36% relative to baseline, demonstrating improved scientific modeling capability. EvoSim turns experimental observations into validated models and cumulative research expertise.

items.title: A Closer Look at Agentic BBO: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Black-Box Optimization
items.excerpt: Black-box optimization (BBO) arises in many scientific and engineering problems where objective evaluations are expensive and limited. Recent large language model (LLM) agents offer a new way to approach BBO by combining task semantics, computation, optimization tools, and feedback-driven decision making, showing great potential due to the integration with mathematically rigorous tools. However, existing agentic BBO studies use different task domains and system configurations, making their results difficult to compare and the effects of individual design choices hard to isolate. We therefore introduce AgenticBBO-Bench, a cross-domain benchmark for agentic BBO spanning synthetic functions, hyperparameter optimization, database tuning, chip design, and molecular design under a unified finite-budget evaluation protocol. In our experiments, agentic BBO achieves higher family-averaged scores than direct LLM-based methods in all five domains and outperforms the best numerical optimizers in four. We further study three factors shaping agent performance: optimization tools, task information and prior knowledge, and the role of the LLM during search. Our results show that additional numerical tools do not consistently improve performance, task semantics are broadly useful while more specific priors are less reliable, and numerical optimizers can effectively absorb gains from search trajectories established by the agent. Finally, we introduce a five-task frontier challenge within AgenticBBO-Bench and evaluate seven LLMs under the Codex agent harness, where GPT-6 Astra and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash lie on the Pareto frontier of performance and cost among the evaluated models. Our code is available at https://github.com/lamda-bbo/agentic-bbo.
items.summary: 该论文提出跨域基准 AgenticBBO-Bench，在统一预算下系统评估LLM智能体用于黑箱优化，发现其总体优于直接LLM方法并在多数领域超越最佳数值优化器，同时揭示优化工具、任务信息/先验知识与LLM作用等设计因素的影响。

items.title: Language Models as AI Research World Models
items.excerpt: AI research agents automate the cycle of proposing, implementing, and evaluating experiments, opening a path toward recursive self-improvement. Yet their ability to propose experiments outpaces their capacity to execute them in real environments, making outcome prediction a key capability for sustained self-improvement under limited experimental budgets. We investigate language models as Research World Models (RWMs), which predict the outcomes of candidate interventions across research environments. Our evaluation draws on over 2,600 experimental records from nine research environments spanning pretraining, post-training, and inference, representing more than 171,000 H100 GPU-hours of experimentation. Research knowledge acquired from real experimental experience improves RWM predictions of unseen interventions within the same environment (Spearman +0.27), and can be reused across environments. For example, using only pretraining experience from OLMo3, Marin, and Nanochat, an RWM reduces selection regret in the Qwen3 environment by 78% compared with zero-experience setting. These benefits extend to multi-round Autoresearch under a fixed selection budget: RWMs with in-env and cross-env research knowledge increase the best gain achieved by 15.8% and 11.6%, respectively. Ablations across 13 language models used as RWMs show that adding research knowledge can improve intervention ranking more than changing models or increasing reasoning effort alone. These findings support language models as RWMs and motivate accumulating experimental data for future RWM training.
items.summary: 语言模型可作为"研究世界模型"来预测候选实验干预的结果，而来自真实实验的研究知识能显著提升其预测精度并跨环境复用，从而在有限实验预算下增强AI自动研究的自我改进能力。

items.title: AtomWorld-Mirror: Macro-Step World Modeling of Critical Evolution Backbones for Materials Dynamics
items.excerpt: Atomistic simulation is a fundamental tool for studying long-term materials evolution, from diffusion and defect dynamics to interfacial reactions and fracture. Yet conventional simulators typically advance at microscopic resolution, spending substantial computation on low-impact local updates before reaching structurally consequential states, an evolutionary-resolution bottleneck that limits long-horizon simulation. We propose AtomWorld-Mirror, a time-aware macro-step world model for the critical evolution backbone of atomic systems. For Step-Wise atomistic simulation, AtomWorld-Mirror distills short micro-event segments into physically reachable transitions between key states, jointly predicting sparse structural edits and accumulated physical time through latent macro-step dynamics. Local reachability, inventory conservation, and continuous-time consistency constrain each transition. By amortizing local atomic physics into a reusable latent macro model and replacing explicit micro-event replay with macro-step inference, this formulation provides a path toward substantially faster prediction of long-term materials evolution while preserving structural validity and time semantics. Across five atomic systems, spanning Cu-rich RPV steel irradiation aging, Cu-Zr metallic glass, and Li$_3$N-based anti-perovskite solid electrolyte, macro-step inference delivers a speed up of $10^3$ to $10^4$ times over event-by-event simulation.
items.summary: 本文提出 AtomWorld-Mirror——一种面向原子系统关键演化骨架的时间感知宏步世界模型，通过将微观事件段蒸馏为关键状态间的物理可达跃迁并联合预测稀疏结构编辑与累积物理时间，在多种材料体系中实现比逐事件模拟快 \(10^3\) 至 \(10^4\) 倍的长时程演化预测。

items.title: $C_4$-Equivariant Flow Matching on Anisotropic Power-Diagram Graphs for Microstructure Generation
items.excerpt: Acquiring realistic microstructure data through Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) is costly and time consuming, often relying on specialised equipment. As microstructures strongly influence material properties, generating realistic samples is essential for modelling the behaviour of polycrystalline materials. We introduce a generative model for synthesising realistic polycrystalline microstructures using flow matching and graph neural networks. By representing microstructures as anisotropic power diagrams, our model learns a compact geometric parametrisation and can render generated samples at arbitrary pixel resolution. A $C_4$-equivariant architecture incorporates rotational symmetry directly into the model, ensuring that rotations of the input noise produce corresponding rotations of the generated microstructure. We also demonstrate how training-free guidance can be used to generate complex microstructures, based on user defined objective function. In particular, we generate microstructures resembling a copper weld, cast metal slab, 3D-printed stainless steel and heterogeneous lamella titanium.

items.title: PXtal: Learning to Align Powder X-Ray Diffraction and Crystal Structures under Information Asymmetry across Modalities
items.excerpt: Scientific multimodal learning commonly assumes that paired views are comparably informative. Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) makes this mismatch explicit: compressing a three-dimensional crystal structure into a one-dimensional diffraction pattern loses information and makes the pattern harder to connect to the crystal structure that produced it. We introduce PXtal, a framework for learning aligned PXRD and crystal representations under this physically imposed information asymmetry. PXtal uses Unbalanced Optimal Transport (UOT) to adapt the cross-modal coupling and coupling-level generalized Kullback-Leibler (GKL) divergence to supervise the full transport plan. Across six test sets, including four zero-shot transfer sets, PXtal consistently outperforms the baseline models in PXRD-to-crystal candidate retrieval, with the largest gains when PXRD patterns have close but crystallographically distinct nonpaired neighbors, meaning similar input patterns associated with different crystals. The resulting crystal and PXRD encoders transfer more effectively to downstream materials and crystallographic tasks. These results identify information asymmetry as a general design problem in scientific multimodal learning: alignment objectives should reflect what each modality preserves.
items.summary: PXtal 针对粉末X射线衍射（PXRD）到晶体结构映射中固有的信息不对称，利用非平衡最优传输（UOT）和耦合级GKL散度对齐两种模态的表示，从而显著提升PXRD到晶体候选检索及下游材料任务的性能。

items.title: Generation, Accumulation, and Utilization of Data in the Automatically Controlled End-Station of a Soft X-ray Beamline
items.excerpt: AI is rapidly transforming materials exploration, yet reliable AI-assisted research depends on experimental data that retains their context, provenance, and machine-readable structure. High-throughput synchrotron measurements therefore require more than automated data acquisition: data generation, accumulation, and utilization must be connected within a continuous workflow. Here, we present a data-centric research framework that integrates the PIONEER system, the OMNES, and ML analysis. The PIONEER system automates sample handling, vacuum transfer, and scanning XAS at the BL08U soft X-ray beamline of NanoTerasu, systematically generating large volumes of spatially resolved spectral data. Measurement and analysis files are stored in the cloud-based ARIM-mdx data system, while OMNES manages metadata describing samples, preparation procedures, measurement conditions, instrument settings, data locations, and analysis histories. Tabular and JavaScript Object Notation formats are used according to the metadata structure, with numerical values stored separately from units to facilitate machine processing. OMNES organizes these records based on causal relationships among experimental and analytical processes, linking samples, measurements, raw data, processed data, and analysis results through a relational data model and visualizing their relationships as a graph. This causality-based organization preserves experimental and analytical provenance and clarifies how each result was derived from the preceding processes and data. The accumulated spectra can subsequently be processed using ML methods, including dimensionality reduction and materials classification, and the resulting data can be registered back into OMNES. Previously reported ML analysis of BN XAS spectra is presented as an example of the analytical workflow that can be applied to data acquired at the beamline.
items.summary: 该论文提出一个以数据为中心的工作流框架，将PIONEER自动化测量系统、OMNES元数据与因果溯源管理以及机器学习分析整合于NanoTerasu BL08U软X射线光束线，实现高通量XAS数据的自动生成、云端积累、可溯源管理和再利用。

items.title: Data driven screening of CaCu$_5$-type magnetic structures
items.excerpt: We develop a machine learning assisted workflow for the rapid screening of permanent magnet candidates within the CaCu$_5$ structure family. We generated more than 60,000 structures through substitutions. These compositions were screened using a combination of pretrained materials models, Materials Project data, and a machine-learning model for magnetization prediction. Four criteria, namely, metallicity, negative formation energy, energy above the convex hull $\leq 50$~meV/atom, and predicted magnetization above the adopted $\geq 0.75$~T threshold reduced the initial chemical space to 439 candidates for first-principles calculations. Density functional theory calculations revealed that 159 compounds exhibit positive axial magnetic anisotropy energy, favoring [001] over the tested in-plane directions. The resulting dataset reveals chemical trends in magnetic anisotropy across the CaCu$_5$ compositional space and provides a set of candidates for further investigation. More broadly, this work demonstrates a practical strategy for combining existing machine learning models with first-principles calculations to systematically reduce large chemical spaces to tractable sets for computationally intensive materials screening.

items.title: Open-ended Scientific Discovery with Possibilistic Reasoning
items.excerpt: Autonomous scientific discovery with LLMs requires generating and testing hypotheses adaptively as evidence accumulates while maintaining statistical validity. Existing anytime-valid methods can handle data-dependent hypotheses, but open-ended discovery poses a deeper challenge: the best discovered hypothesis may still be the best of a bad lot, with better explanations yet undiscovered, while even background knowledge such as physical laws may require revision in light of new findings. In response, we formalize the problem as Abductive Autonomous Scientific Discovery (AASD) using possibility theory. We introduce abductive utility, a computable measure of discovery progress, and possibility frontier search, the first algorithm for AASD, which maintains anytime validity and achieves $\varepsilon$-optimal abductive utility asymptotically under suitable conditions. Experiments on synthetic and real-world scientific-discovery tasks show strong performance.
items.summary: 本文利用可能性理论形式化开放式自主科学发现（AASD），提出可计算的溯因效用指标与首个算法“可能性前沿搜索”，在保持任意时间有效性的同时渐近达到 ε-最优，并在合成及真实科学发现任务上取得优异表现。

items.title: Is In-Domain Training Enough for Fine-Grained Industrial Anomaly Understanding?
items.excerpt: A single multimodal large language model (MLLM) struggles to excel simultaneously at detection, localization, description, and reasoning in multimodal industrial anomaly understanding (MM-IAU). We show that in-domain training does not close this gap. On MMAD, a widely adopted MM-IAU benchmark, trained specialists reach at most 75.5% accuracy in defect localization, against 92.3% for human experts, and even detect anomalies less accurately than their untrained base model. Meanwhile, different MLLMs offer complementary strengths but share this weakness in fine-grained perception, so combining them alone cannot remove it. We therefore propose SiGMA, a spatially grounded multi-agent framework that divides labor between heterogeneous MLLM agents and a dedicated visual defect expert. A multimodal searcher supplies industrial knowledge and normal references, the defect expert turns query-reference comparison into calibrated anomaly evidence, and a label-free reliability controller weighs each source by task-wise competence and query-level evidence quality. SiGMA reaches 85.2% average accuracy on MMAD, 4.0% above the strongest trained specialist and Gemini-2.5-Pro and within 1.5% of human experts. Even with three agents of at most 9B parameters, it reaches 84.4%, and new MLLMs join without retraining.
items.summary: 该论文指出仅靠域内训练不足以实现细粒度工业异常理解，并提出空间接地的多智能体框架 SiGMA，通过异构 MLLM 智能体、专用视觉缺陷专家、多模态检索与无标签可靠性控制器协同，在 MMAD 基准上达到 85.2% 平均准确率，接近人类专家水平。

items.title: LLM-IDEA: Identifiability-Driven Experimental Agent for Autonomous Discovery of Mechanistic World Models
items.excerpt: Large language model agents are being increasingly deployed as autonomous scientists, designing experiments and inferring mechanistic world models with minimal human oversight. Yet identifiability is often overlooked: when a plateau is reached, the agent needs to know whether it is not yet capable enough or the model simply is not identifiable from the data, in which case no amount of further experimentation of the same kind can help. We propose the Identifiability-Driven Experimental Agent (LLM-IDEA) for closed-loop discovery with an identifiability engine that returns a three-way plateau verdict: capability limit, resolvable within the design class, or certified exhausted. On ODEBench, 60 of the 62 systems with free constants are identifiable at round 0; the RC circuit is certified exhausted for every experiment that protocol can run, and a harvesting model is resolvable by one added initial condition. The identifiability engine reproduces known verdicts on Lotka-Volterra, Van der Pol, Lorenz, and a pharmacokinetic model, where it recommends the intravenous arm pharmacologists use, and it ranks the depth scorer of our own benchmark last among four observation designs. On the DiscoverPhysics benchmark, it finds two public worlds whose explanation rubric rewards a distinction no legal experiment can make, and every model there with accurate trajectories failed the explanation grade (15 of 15, against 5 of 9 in identifiable worlds, p = 0.012). On the Alien Universe, a two-body testbed we propose in which a force law switches between a provably non-identifiable and an identifiable protocol, LLM-IDEA on the identifiable protocol reaches discovery depth at least three on 8/8 seeds versus 1/8 without it. An autonomous discovery agent can thus compute, rather than guess, whether a plateau calls for more search, a better experiment of the same kind, or a different kind of experiment.
items.summary: LLM-IDEA 通过可辨识性引擎判断实验平台期是能力不足、设计类内可解决还是已穷尽，使自主智能体能计算而非猜测该继续搜索、改进同类实验还是更换实验类型，从而发现机制世界模型。

items.title: OpenProblemBench: Benchmarking AI on Open Problems in the Foundational Theoretical Sciences
items.excerpt: The next frontier for artificial general intelligence is tackling unresolved scientific problems, calling for benchmarks that assess progress beyond established knowledge. We introduce OpenProblemBench, a benchmark of 82 unresolved problems drawn from the mathematics and theoretical physics literature. Each problem supplies the research context, assumptions, and prior progress needed to investigate the question. We select problems whose proposed solutions admit comparatively clear checks of their decisive mathematical or computational claims. Four evaluator models independently assess the correctness, completeness, and degree of progress of each submission without reference solutions. Across seven evaluated configurations, GPT-6-Astra achieves the highest mean judged solve rate of 14.0%, compared with 5.5-6.7% for the evaluated full-size open models and 2.4-3.7% for Flash models. Case comparisons connect stronger outcomes to changes in problem representation, general arguments that extend beyond finite evidence, and proofs of the steps needed to complete a solution. By grounding evaluation in questions arising from the research literature, OpenProblemBench provides a setting for investigating the capabilities and limitations of AI as a contributor to foundational theoretical science.
items.summary: 该论文提出了 OpenProblemBench——一个包含 82 个数学与理论物理未解问题的基准，用四个评估模型在无参考答案下评判 AI 解答的正确性、完整性与进展，发现最佳配置 GPT-6-Astra 的平均判定解决率仅为 14.0%，表明 AI 在基础理论科学开放问题上仍能力有限。
